Michael Mitzenmacher received the PhD degree in computer science from the University of California, Berkeley, in 1996. From 1996 to 1998, he worked as a researcher at Digital Systems Research Center, now owned by Compaq. In January 1999, he joined Harvard University as an assistant professor of computer science. His research interests focus on random processes and algorithms, including load balancing, algorithms for the Web, network

protocols, stochastic bin packing, coding theory, and compression. He is a member of the IEEE.
